title: Internal modules in abelian groups are ordinary modules
statement: Use the internal-module convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For every ring R in Type u, regard its additive group as a monoid object of Ab with the tensor product over integers. There exists an equivalence functor F from internal R-module objects in Ab to ModuleCat R such that its composite with the forgetful functor to Ab is equal to the internal-module forgetful functor. This includes the zero ring and requires no commutativity or finiteness.

source.place: Section 5.3, pointwise module encoding; agent-expanded tensor universal-property argument

proof.text: Evaluate the internal action on pure tensors to define r • m. The internal unit and associativity equations on 1 tensor m and (r tensor s) tensor m give the module laws; bilinearity gives the additive laws. Evaluating a morphism action equation on pure tensors gives linearity, producing a functor to ModuleCat R.

The ordinary bilinear scalar action factors through the integer tensor product. Its unit and associativity diagrams hold on pure tensors, so it constructs an internal module for each ordinary module. Tensor-product extensionality similarly lifts every ordinary linear map. This proves fullness and faithfulness of the first functor.

For every ordinary module, the inverse construction followed by the first functor has the same action, so identity on the underlying group gives an ordinary linear isomorphism. Thus the functor is essentially surjective and an equivalence. Its composite forgetful functor is definitionally the internal-module forgetful functor.
